name: Peachbeige
lede: Peachbeige is a warm, sandy tan between peach and beige, a 1928 fashion-trade name from the Maerz and Paul dictionary.

sections.title: A trade name, not a flower or place
sections.body:
The nearest named colors on file are [[tumbleweed]], [[pastel-parchment]] and [[yellowish-camel]], at 2.6, 3.1 and 3.8 ΔE [1]. Running the two words together, rather than writing "peach beige," marks it as a single fixed trade term rather than a description built on the spot [1].

Its Munsell notation is 6.1YR 7.1/4.9, and the closest of our common colors is [[camel]], 6.2 units away, with its nearest library neighbor being [[tumbleweed]] [1]. Nothing in the books we hold explains who coined it [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
In our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, this tan appears in 1,223, about 5.1 percent, more common than 87 percent of our named colors [2]. It peaks in the 1500s, in 110 of 2,231 paintings, at 1.6 times the expected rate, and it is most over-represented in paintings from India, at 2.8 times the expected rate [2].

[[painter:andre-derain|Andre Derain]] is its most devoted painter, present in 5 of 22 works here, 4.3 times his museums' baseline [2]. The earliest match is a 900-era painting, over a thousand years before the 1928 name, so that early hit is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not a trace of this named tan, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. It shares canvases more than chance with [[seashell-pink]] and [[french-beige]] [2].

origin.named_after: undocumented; a fashion-trade compound of peach and beige
